summary:
### TL;DR
- **Dependabot alerts will be turned off on inactive repositories starting December 8, 2026.** This affects most repos with no activity in the past year. Their alerts are archived, not deleted, and can be restored. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-10-dependabot-alerts-will-pause-on-inactive-repositories))
- **Gemini 4 Carbon is now generally available in GitHub Copilot.** New models are auto-enabled under default model enablement, so Business and Enterprise admins should check their model policy if they restrict models. ([changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-10-gemini-4-carbon-in-github-copilot))
- **GitHub Advanced Security (GHAS) trial eligibility has been broadened in the docs.** Several prerequisites were removed: payment method, the 300-seat cap, and no prior purchase or paid license. ([docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/trialing-github-advanced-security/trial-advanced-security))
- No GitHub Actions-specific changes appeared in this period.

### Action required
- **Dependabot alerts pause on inactive repos (effective December 8, 2026).** ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-10-dependabot-alerts-will-pause-on-inactive-repositories))
  - **What counts as activity:** pushing to any branch or tag, creating the repository, or turning on Dependabot alerts.
  - **Who is affected:** all plans on github.com and GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency. GitHub Enterprise Server is not affected.
  - **Repos that are exempt:**
    - Repos with an enforced security configuration that enables Dependabot alerts.
    - Repos in enterprises whose Dependabot alerts policy doesn't let repository admins enable or disable alerts.
  - **What to do:** If you have low-activity repos that still matter, such as archived-but-deployed libraries or stable internal tools, apply an enforced security configuration or the appropriate enterprise policy before December 8.
  - **Recovery:** Any push or a manual re-enable in repository settings restores the archived alerts and resets the one-year clock.

### Security improvements
- **Copilot model governance (Gemini 4 Carbon).**
  - The model is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users across IDEs, the CLI, the coding agent, github.com, and mobile.
  - It is described as focused on secure code generation and security-focused work.
  - It is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing.
  - Admins manage access through the Copilot model policy. It is enabled automatically unless the global default is off or the model is explicitly disabled.
  - Rollout is gradual. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-10-gemini-4-carbon-in-github-copilot))
- No other new security capabilities were announced. The C++ language server MSBuild auto-configuration change is a developer-tooling update with no security impact. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-10-c-language-server-now-auto-configures-msbuild-builds))

### Docs changes worth reading
- **GHAS trial eligibility criteria were relaxed** across two commits ([commit 1](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/b66175924ad9ccefdbbdf3c6146cf02561787d43), [commit 2](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/d8da2b9da5a2b9394bb83300060d8276e1766c64); [page](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/trialing-github-advanced-security/trial-advanced-security)).
  - **Removed requirements:**
    - Paying by credit card or PayPal. The "pay by invoice: contact sales" tip was also removed.
    - Having an enterprise with 300 or fewer seats.
    - Not having previously purchased GHAS or held a paid license.
  - **Remaining criteria:**
    - You are an enterprise account owner.
    - You are not already using metered billing for GHAS.
    - You have had at most one previous GHAS trial, and it ended at least 180 days ago.
  - **Why it matters:** Larger, invoice-billed, or previously licensed enterprises may now be able to self-serve a GHAS trial.

changelog.title: Gemini 4 Carbon in GitHub Copilot
changelog.text: Gemini 4 Carbon, Google’s latest model, is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. It is designed for complex coding, agentic, and reasoning tasks, with a focus on secure code generation and security-focused work. This model is billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing. See Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot for details. Availability in GitHub Copilot Gemini 4 Carbon is available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users. You can select the model in the model picker in: Visual Studio Code Visual Studio Copilot CLI GitHub Copilot coding agent GitHub Copilot app github.com GitHub Mobile on iOS and Android JetBrains IDEs Xcode Eclipse Rollout will be gradual. Check back soon if you don’t see it yet. Enabling access Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business plan administrators can manage access to Gemini 4 Carbon through the model policy in Copilot settings. Under default model enablement, new models are automatically enabled unless an administrator has turned off the global default or explicitly disables this model. Learn more To explore all models available in GitHub Copilot, see our documentation on models and get started with Copilot. Share your feedback Join the GitHub Community to share your feedback. The post Gemini 4 Carbon in GitHub Copilot appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: C++ language server now auto-configures MSBuild builds
changelog.text: The Microsoft C++ Language Server for GitHub Copilot CLI now bundles its MSBuild compile commands extractor and invokes it automatically. An agent no longer needs to discover and run a separate configuration skill before it can get precise code intelligence for your project. For more information, including the installation instructions, see the main repository page . What changed Previously, setting up go-to-definition, find references, and other language server features for an MSBuild-based C++ project required you to either provide your own compile_commands.json file or Copilot to locate and run a configuration skill before it could generate a compilation database. That extra discovery step added setup time and consumed tokens before Copilot could start working with your code. Now: The compile commands extractor is bundled directly with the C++ language server, so it’s always available. Copilot invokes the extractor when starting the language server on project open, with no manual or agent-driven setup skill required. Compilation database generation for MSBuild projects is deterministic, reducing setup token usage. Configure other build systems For other build systems, you can provide your own compile_commands.json or use a skill to generate one: For CMake projects, use the generate compile commands skill introduced in the earlier C++ language server release by asking Copilot CLI to “load project.” For custom build systems, follow the guide to create a custom build extractor skill . Get started Follow the Microsoft C++ Language Server quick start to install the plugin and accept the EULA. If your repository contains an MSBuild-based C++ project, Copilot will automatically generate the compilation database it needs for accurate code intelligence. An active GitHub Copilot subscription is required. Help improve the Microsoft C++ Language Server by completing the C++ language server survey . To report a problem or suggest an improvement, open an issue in the Microsoft C++ Language Server repository . The post C++ language server now auto-configures MSBuild builds appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Dependabot alerts will pause on inactive repositories
changelog.text: Starting December 8, 2026, GitHub will turn off Dependabot alerts on most repositories with no activity in the past year. Their existing alerts are archived, not deleted, and you can restore them at any time. With vulnerability discovery and alert volume growing quickly, this keeps Dependabot fast and reliable for the repositories you’re actively developing. What counts as activity GitHub counts any of these as activity: Pushing to any branch or tag Creating the repository Turning on Dependabot alerts Turn alerts back on Any push to the repository automatically turns Dependabot alerts back on. You can also turn them on in the repository’s settings . Either way, GitHub restores the archived alerts, and the one-year clock starts over. Keep alerts on regardless of activity GitHub won’t turn off alerts on repositories with an enforced security configuration that enables Dependabot alerts. It also skips repositories in enterprises whose Dependabot alerts policy doesn’t allow repository administrators to enable or disable alerts. This change applies to all plans on github.com and to GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency. For data residency customers, archived alerts are stored in the same region as the rest of your enterprise’s data. It doesn’t apply to GitHub Enterprise Server. The post Dependabot alerts will pause on inactive repositories appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
